As the sun sets, the armored urchin slowly crawls out of the water with its long repurposed spines, perching itself on rocky outcrops to 
open its clam-like lid to reveal the waving luminescent tendrils within. Motes of glowing bacteria flow within the transparent skin of 
the tendrils as they wave back and forth in the gloom of the dusk light like a nest of worms to catch the eye of the high flying sea birds. 
Once sighted, they quickly descend to pluck the little wriggling lures, just as their beak nearly closes in on the glowing lures, the lid 
snaps shut with shocking force. Th ese tendrils are coated in a paralyzing neurotoxin that numbs the flesh of their victim and stills their 
thrashing struggle, while the hard calcite teeth of the urchin slowly grinds the immobilized prey to a grizzly end.
Class - Echinoidea • Genus Derived Evolution - Colobocentrotus • Niche - Specialist Carnivore
Preyed upon by - Daugon, Gharril, Slannethiss, Vortautilus • Preys on - Black Billed Fingulls

Clamping Shell Th e trikautrae can close its shell. While closed 
it gains +2 AC (total 16) and Resistance to Piercing and Slashing

A swallowed creature has the Paralyzed and Restrained

If the trikautrae dies, any swallowed creature no longer has the

Encountering. Along the rocky shores of the Strands, the 
trikautrae is often found nestled among the stones and tidal 
pools. Never venturing far from the water, it often comes 
ashore at night, opening its wide mouth to entrap prey with 
its luminescent glowing tendrils that wave in the moonlit air. 
During the day, nestled among the clams and stones, it is much 
harder to spot.

Defensive Instinct When near death, its shell closes against intrusion.
